title: Fpqc sheaf condition from Zariski descent and affine singleton covers
statement: In fixed universes [def-weil-size-convention], let $F:(\mathit{Sch})^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathit{Sets}$ be a contravariant set-valued functor on schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Then $F$ satisfies the sheaf condition for every fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] if and only if both of the following hold: (1) $F$ satisfies the Zariski sheaf property [def-pc-zariski-sheaf-property]; (2) for every fpqc covering consisting of one morphism $f:T\prime\to T$ with both schemes affine (each isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative ring), $F(T)\to F(T\prime)$ is the equalizer of $F(T\prime)\rightrightarrows F(T\prime\times_TT\prime)$, with the two arrows given by restriction along the projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. In the first assertion, the sheaf condition means that a family of sections over the members of any fpqc covering, agreeing after both projections to every pairwise overlap, is the restriction of exactly one section over its target.

source.place: Tag 022H, lemma-sheaf-property-fpqc, including the equivalence of (2) and (2-prime).

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: set P = AlgebraicGeometry.Flat in SheafQuasiCompact.lean:36-41 and rewrite Scheme.fpqcTopology_eq_propQCTopology (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Fpqc.lean:78). The result is exactly Zariski descent plus singleton flat surjections Spec B -> Spec A. Every affine scheme is isomorphic to a spectrum, and on affine schemes a flat surjection is exactly a singleton fpqc covering. The Flat instances required are HasRingHomProperty (Morphisms/Flat.lean:54, inducing locality), IsMultiplicative (line 78), and isStableUnderBaseChange (line 81); all are existing instances. The matching-family/equalizer formulation is Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff_pullbacks (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/IsSheafFor.lean:968-972), specialized to a singleton. No additional geometric hypothesis is needed.
